extracted.intended_audience: individuals, organizations, and representatives who want to submit public comments on federal regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing and submitting public comments to federal agencies during notice-and-comment rulemaking, including who may comment, timing, submission channels, content quality, and technical/file requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can comment / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual, organization, non-profit, lobbying group, or federal agency with legitimate interest — anonymously or through a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may be submitted by a wide range of actors; anonymous submissions are permitted and representatives may file on behalf of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period and statutory timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: 60-day comment period (7 PM ET written / 11:59 PM ET digital deadlines). Agencies must allow a 30-day reply period and must address public feedback in final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the published comment period and exact deadline times (written vs. digital). Expect agencies to respond and account for comments when drafting final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods / channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Four Submission Methods: Federal Register (regulations.gov) — most common; agency websites; by mail — postmarked by deadline and include docket/rule ID; in-person hearings — when scheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate channel (regulations.gov is typical). For mailed comments ensure postmark by deadline and include the docket/rule ID so the agency can associate your comment; attend in-person hearings if oral comment is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include identifying information for the regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include identifying information for the regulation — name and docket ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always state the rule name and docket or rule ID clearly at the top of your submission so the agency can correctly file and consider your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish credibility and support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish credibility — ground comments in relevant expertise/experience, supported by research and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant research, data, or firsthand experience to support assertions; indicate your qualifications or stake when relevant to strengthen persuasive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear structure, precise language, and focused objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear structure — define objectives, precise language, supporting evidence, citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the comment with a clear statement of requested action or change, present evidence logically, avoid vague language, and include citations for referenced facts or studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/file upload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: File uploads limited to 20 attachments, 10MB max each. Accepted formats: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .jpg, .png, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare attachments within size/format limits; combine documents where appropriate to stay under attachment and size caps and prefer widely accepted formats like PDF or DOCX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing-specific procedural requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments sent by mail must be postmarked by the deadline and include the docket/rule ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using postal submission, verify postmark rules and include the docket/rule ID on the envelope and in the comment so it will be accepted and docketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking submitted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can be tracked via regulations.gov's help section under 'find a comment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, use regulations.gov tools to confirm receipt and view public posting; tracking helps verify the comment was docketed and monitor agency responses.
